correctness.rationale: The explicit strip intersection has exactly the six asserted extreme vertices; exact positive unit-normal moment weights certify the John unit disk and exact positive vertex moment weights certify the proposed Löwner ellipse. Affine covariance gives commutator entry -3/130. The already-proved continuous uniqueness of maximal-intersection ellipses extends noncommutation from endpoint matrices to two strictly interior areas. Quarter-turn uniqueness for a square and affine covariance exclude all centrally symmetric quadrilaterals. A standalone Fraction checker reproduces every nonstandard rational contact identity and the vertex census; no finite numerical experiment is being mistaken for the continuity theorem.

originality.rationale: The exact rational six-vertex and contact-weight construction and minimality claim are not stated or implied by the relevant examined primary results. Bochi supplies general uniqueness/continuity and a smooth quartic example, not a certified minimal polygon counterexample; the other indexed statements concern distinct objects or invariants. An imperfect search cannot establish absolute priority, and residual risks are disclosed.
residual_risks: A differently indexed historical example of noncoaxial John/Löwner ellipses of a centrally symmetric hexagon could exist; no absolute novelty proof is claimed.
Bochi Figure 1 already addresses generic non-symmetric MI positions on a smooth body; this work claims only exact polygonal minimality and its rational certificate.
The current semantic search is not exhaustive, and a full systematic survey of all John–Löwner shape-operator literature has not been made.
No independent expert validation or external audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The motivating structural question is whether fixed-area maximal-intersection ellipses retain a common orthogonal principal-axis system as area changes. The exact noncoaxial construction at the first possible centrally symmetric vertex count, together with a no-four-vertex theorem, determines the smallest polygonal geometric complexity for failure. This is not merely a coordinate rescaling or a routine negative normal-form check: two distinct optimal endpoint certificates and a nonzero commutator are necessary to make the interpolating family change axes.
